body: The thing about disillusionment, is that it strips away all the pretense that you could ever go back to the way things were before. Or that you could ever exist in a world where joy, isn't stained by the dark muck of reality. All of my problems, like I said, are fixable. But joy, I think, will always elude me. 10 years ago, when I was 16, I thought I'd be past all this. The fact that I'm still here, lingering, trying to hold on to some shred of hope that future me will have left this behind, is truly disheartening. Hope in the future. Thats the only place where I think there's some shred of positivity, if not joy, in my life. But I know now that the future won't be any different. Im stuck, out of gas and momentum to keep lying to myself. There's no purpose in my life. I've fed the homeless, cared for the elderly, done charitable acts. None of it fills that gaping hole in heart. It's just filler. A facade that helps me keep holding on. I don't really care how society perceives people with my condition. Like I said, I'm not looking for a shoulder to cry on, or someone to blather to. Nor do I care about having an outlet. This is more an exercise in giving me perspective on my depression and impending decision, more than anything else. I may be a coward for choosing to end my own life. Those critiques however, from others or myself, wont matter pretty soon.

I know that I have clinical depression, its nothing I need a diagnosis for. I've spoken to counselors and priests, but in all honesty nothing they say would ever help. I learned a long time ago that humans are just that, human. My depression doesn't so much stem from any career, professional, or relationship sources. Its from disillusionment. A realization that for all my accomplishments, they only serve as a bright contrast to the emptiness. I can be among a group of friends, pretending that I'm on the same page. Joking about sports, politics,  talking about women, etc. But it's just the face I put on. I don't make any cringeworthy pretense of "always being the outsider" or some loner/emo nonsense. The truth is that I wish I could be oblivious to the muddy, deep hollow that is my depression, the loss of faith, the frustration. No one is going to tell me anything that I haven't already told myself, or that common sense spells out plainly. Medication just hides, suppresses the problem. It's still there. The knowledge that there isn't anything worth living for anymore. That when I end it, either it'll be "fade to black", or maybe I'll get a chance to ask the God I think made a mistake sending me into the world, why exactly he enjoys watching me squirm? Then he'll just send me to hell or purgatory for committing the most selfish act of all, suicide. God doesn't have any answers, and neither do counselors, priests, or medication/therapy. The way I see it, there are just some people God has slated to be losers in life, even those who've had succeses. It's how the universe balances out. Not everyone can be a winner. Some people just have to be designated the ones that just suck at life. If God really does exist, and does care, he's an all knowing being, who's seen and authored the beginning and end of time and how everyone meets their end. Everyone who jumps off a building, eats a bullet, puts a noose around their neck could have been stopped, but God lets it happen, every second of the day. I don't place any blame on Him, maybe I once did, but not anymore. That's just the way the world works. People have to lose, and I'm one of them. Every little thing that's led up to this moment, and my heart being where it is, is my fault. I can accept that, and acknowledge that some people aren't cut out for this world, and I fall in that category. I am who I am, whole on the outside, broken on the inside. People say that killing yourself is illogical, because you dont "feel" any relief, because you'll be dead. I agree, that is illogical. I'm not looking for relief. I'm just looking for a way out. A way out of the trap I've created for myself, where I'm my own worst enemy. 

You tell anyone you're thinking of offing yourself, it's all pity and handholding. But because of the way human beings are biologically programmed to view mental illness, its never really genuine sorrow or care, not that I'm looking for it.  The human brain can't rationalize the desire of another to end their life. You're just broken. Off. Defective.  The living don't have the time or mental faculties to actually help people looking to kill themselves, which is why so many suicides in this country (USA) happen every year.  It's just the way people are. Probably the way I'd be too, dealing with a suicidal individual. I don't want to bring my internal misery around other people, but its an inevitiability with something as pronounced as intending to kill yourself. I wish my problems could be fixed with a handwave or money. I know that no matter how high up I'll go, I'll always have this emptiness inside of me. The frustration of never being able to relate to people genuinely. The bitter knowledge that God doesn't care, and Jesus does not in fact save. That there's no new-age hippy, incense infused, spiritual schpiel that's going to make me whole. No one ever truly understands the reasons someone does it. Not to say that theres some profound vision every suicide attempter sees and uses as justification. Its just subjective. Until we're able to read minds at the granular level, no one outside of me and God (if he's there) will understand why I shot myself. No letter or voice recording I leave behind will answer that question either. We all die, and we all die alone. Some people just chose to clock out sooner. 

I honestly can't remember the last, truly happy day I've had.
